module_title: Kinetic Theory, Real Gases & Crystal Geometry (Intermediate)
introduction: This level transitions to the microscopic Kinetic Theory of Gases (KTG) and the corrections required for Real Gases (van der Waals). It also covers complex solid-state geometries, calculating packing efficiencies, identifying voids, and utilizing the density formula for crystal lattices.

core_concepts.title: Kinetic Theory of Gases (KTG) & Molecular Speeds
core_concepts.description:
Postulates of KTG: Gas molecules are point masses with negligible volume, and there are no intermolecular forces between them. 
Three types of molecular speeds (Derived from Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution):
1. Root Mean Square Speed: $v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{3RT/M}$.
2. Average Speed: $v_{\text{avg}} = \sqrt{8RT/\pi M}$.
3. Most Probable Speed: $v_{\text{mp}} = \sqrt{2RT/M}$.
Ratio: $v_{\text{mp}} : v_{\text{avg}} : v_{\text{rms}} = 1 : 1.128 : 1.224$ (RAM rule: $R > A > M$).

core_concepts.title: Real Gases and Compressibility Factor ($Z$)
core_concepts.description:
Real gases deviate from ideal behavior at High Pressure and Low Temperature because molecules have finite volume and exhibit attractive forces. The Compressibility Factor is $Z = PV/nRT$.
- If $Z = 1$: Ideal behavior.
- If $Z < 1$: Negative deviation (Attractive forces dominate, gas is more compressible, typical at moderate pressures).
- If $Z > 1$: Positive deviation (Repulsive forces dominate, gas is less compressible, typical at high pressures for all gases, and at all pressures for $H_2$ and $He$).

core_concepts.title: van der Waals Equation
core_concepts.description:
Corrects the ideal gas equation for real gases: $\left(P + \frac{an^2}{V^2}\right)(V - nb) = nRT$.
- Constant '$a$' corrects for intermolecular forces (pressure correction). Higher '$a$' means easily liquefiable gas (e.g., $NH_3, SO_2$).
- Constant '$b$' corrects for the finite volume of gas molecules (volume correction, co-volume). $b = 4 \times \text{volume of one mole of molecules}$.

core_concepts.title: Packing Efficiency & Atomic Radius ($r$) vs Edge Length ($a$)
core_concepts.description:
1. Simple Cubic (SC): Atoms touch along the edge. $a = 2r$. Packing Efficiency = $52.4\%$.
2. Body-Centered Cubic (BCC): Atoms touch along the body diagonal. $\sqrt{3}a = 4r$. Packing Efficiency = $68\%$.
3. Face-Centered Cubic (FCC): Atoms touch along the face diagonal. $\sqrt{2}a = 4r$. Packing Efficiency = $74\%$ (Maximum possible packing for spheres of same size).

core_concepts.title: Voids (Interstitial Spaces)
core_concepts.description:
Empty spaces left between packed spheres. If the number of closely packed spheres in an FCC lattice is $N$:
1. Octahedral Voids (OV): Formed by 6 spheres. Number of OVs = $N$. Located at edge centers and body center.
2. Tetrahedral Voids (TV): Formed by 4 spheres. Number of TVs = $2N$. Located on the body diagonals.

core_concepts.title: Density of a Unit Cell
core_concepts.description: The formula connecting macroscopic density with microscopic crystal parameters is: $d = \frac{Z \cdot M}{N_A \cdot a^3}$, where $Z$ is the effective number of atoms, $M$ is molar mass, $N_A$ is Avogadro's number, and $a$ is the edge length of the unit cell.

important_entities.name: Graham's Law of Effusion/Diffusion
important_entities.significance: The rate of effusion or diffusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its molar mass. Lighter gases travel faster. Rate ($r$) can be expressed as Volume/time ($V/t$), Moles/time ($n/t$), or Distance/time ($d/t$). Master equation: $\frac{r_1}{r_2} = \sqrt{\frac{M_2}{M_1}}$.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In the density formula $d = \frac{Z \cdot M}{N_A \cdot a^3}$, the edge length '$a$' is almost always given in picometers ($\text{pm}$) or Angstroms ($\text{\AA}$). Density ($d$) is usually asked in $\text{g/cm}^3$. You MUST convert '$a$' to centimeters before cubing it. $1 \text{ pm} = 10^{-10} \text{ cm}$. Failing to do this will result in answers off by powers of 10.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Octa is Edge-Body, Tetra is Body-Diagonal
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: In an FCC unit cell (which has 4 atoms, $Z=4$), there are exactly 4 Octahedral Voids (located at the 12 edge centers contributing $1/4$ each, plus 1 completely inside at the body center). There are 8 Tetrahedral Voids, located exactly at the 8 corners of a smaller internal cube (2 on each body diagonal).

exam_strategy_tips: For molecular speed problems: Be exceptionally careful with the unit of Molar Mass ($M$). In the formula $v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{3RT/M}$, because $R$ is in Joules ($\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2} \text{K}^{-1}$), $M$ MUST be strictly in $\text{kg/mol}$, not $\text{g/mol}$. E.g., for $O_2$, use $M = 32 \times 10^{-3} \text{ kg/mol}$. If you use 32, your speed will be completely wrong.
